title: Hot-Swap Seller Toolkit (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a concise, field-friendly toolkit for sellers and SEs to run a fast ‘hot-swap’ during pilot or production incidents: a set of compact slides, one-page decision heuristics, and live command-of-conversation scripts to swap models, routes, or capacity tiers with minimal customer disruption.

Context / problem we solve:
- Customers run inference pipelines with strict latency SLAs but sometimes need to shift (hot-swap) to alternative model variants or fallback routing when performance or cost spikes.
- SEs need a short, credible set of moves they can execute in a 15–30 minute call with engineering stakeholders.
- This doc is intentionally lightweight: quick decisions, minimal tech pre-reqs, and clear messaging to procurement/infra.

Primary audience:
- Sales Engineers (SEs) and Platform Sellers who support pilot -> pilot-to-prod conversions.
- Customer platform engineers and site reliability/capacity leads.

How to use:
- Lead with the 2-slide elevator: Why hot-swap matters (latency continuity + cost control) and the 3-move play.
- Keep the one-pager decision map visible during calls.
- Use the sample scripts verbatim when addressing procurement/security concerns.

Topline claim (one-liner for slide):
- "Hot-swap: keep user latency steady and unit cost predictable — three moves to swap models, routes, or capacity in minutes without rewriting app logic."

3 quick plays (rank-ordered):
1) Model variant swap (fastest, least infra friction)
   - What: route to a smaller/quantized variant of the same model family with conservative temperature/beam settings.
   - When: latency has regressed > p90 target but accuracy drop tolerable for short window.
   - Seller script: "We can switch traffic to the 8-bit variant for 10–15% lower p95 — same API surface, no code change."

2) Routing fallback (policy-level)
   - What: change routing policy to prefer regionally cheaper capacity or a different instance pool.
   - When: capacity contended in a region, or spikes causing tail latency — need to preserve correctness.
   - Seller script: "We’ll reroute to our dedicated pool in a nearby region and keep the same model; this reduces queuing without an SDK change."

3) Reserved burst activation (capacity-level)
   - What: temporarily bump reserved capacity or enable burst capacity for the account.
   - When: predictable short-term traffic event (campaign launch).
   - Seller script: "We can flip on burst capacity for the launch window — SLA stays intact, we bill the delta to the reserved commit."

Decision map (one-pager for customers) — read left to right:
- Symptom: latency spike? -> If p95 > target and correctness ok -> Model variant swap.
- Symptom: queueing/502s -> Routing fallback to dedicated region.
- Symptom: planned peak -> Reserved burst activation + schedule rollback.
- If accuracy/relevance degrade -> rollback to prior model and open a problem ticket with Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "Won’t this break quality?" -> "We keep a small % live traffic on the fallback for the first 5–10 minutes; we run a quick smoothed metric check and then graduate the change if signals look clean."
- "I can’t change routing due to compliance" -> "We can scope to a VPC-only private deployment or limit to 'same-country' regions; also propose an offline A/B for 1k requests to validate."
- "How will billing look?" -> "We provide a one-line delta estimate up-front: per-minute cost of burst + marginal tokens for variant. We’ll put a hard stop time in the change ticket."

Slide-by-slide minimal deck (6 slides) — copy/paste-ready:
1) Title + quick claim + one-line customer impact (latency/cost).
2) Problem statement: typical pilot failure modes (latency, cold starts, regional contention).
3) The 3-move hot-swap play (visual flow).
4) Quick decision map (one-pager).
5) Live swap checklist + rollback indicators (metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99, errors, entropy of outputs).
6) Next steps & CTA (schedule canary, optionally reserve burst).

Live metrics checklist (what SE watches during swap):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99, request queue length
- Errors: 5xx rate, retry counts
- Output sanity: token-length distribution, top-k token overlap with baseline sample set
- Cost delta: cost/min and projected hourly spend if held open

Operational TODO for SE before a hot-swap call:
- Confirm customer’s pinned model version and any hard constraints (region, data residency).
- Get baseline perf graphs for last 72h (p95, throughput).
- Prep 2-minute demo of switching to quantized variant in sandbox (show zero-code change).
- Draft rollback commit time and who signs off (customer SRE + Redwood on-call).

Canary recipe (15 minute window):
- Step 0: snapshot baseline metrics & sample prompts (store in ephemeral folder).
- Step 1: shift 5% traffic for 3 minutes -> watch p95 + error rate.
- Step 2: if stable, move to 25% for 5 minutes -> re-evaluate output quality.
- Step 3: full cutover (or rollback) with 10-minute hold to validate downstream systems.

Sample talk track (for a 10m call):
- 0:00–1:00: Confirm SLA & constraints.
- 1:00–3:00: Show baseline perf and propose move (model variant / route / burst).
- 3:00–6:00: Walk through canary & safety gates (what we watch and auto-rollback triggers).
- 6:00–9:00: Execute (we’ll flip 5% now), watch together, propose full cut at minute 9 if stable.
- 9:00–10:00: Next steps (schedule follow-up + ticket).

One-page technical appendix (for SE reference):
- API change surface: none for model variant swap; routing change uses "routingPolicyId" toggle; reserved burst activates via console commit or API flag.
- Telemetry hooks: tag the swap with correlation-id and add a trace span for rollback window.
- Quick CLI snippets: (pseudocode)
   - swap model: redwood.models.route_update(account, route_id, {"model": "mymodel-quant-8bit"})
   - routing fallback: redwood.routes.update(route_id, {"preferred_pools": ["dedicated-eu-1"]})
   - enable burst: redwood.capacity.activate_burst(account, minutes=60)

Open questions / risks to surface to the customer ahead of any swap:
- Are there regulatory constraints on routing across regions? (If yes, default to private deployment options.)
- Any downstream caching or client-side dedup that assumes deterministic tokenization?
- Contractual notice needed for reserved capacity changes?

Local action items (owners):
- Diego: build 2-slide demo sandbox and record a 90s GIF (due 2026-02-20).
- Priya: draft customer-facing one-pager and billing delta template (due 2026-02-18).
- Claire: run 2 internal dry-runs with Platform SEs and get checklist feedback (due 2026-02-25).

Appendix: rapid cheat sheets (copyable lines)
- "We’ll shift 5% now and validate p95 and errors for 3 minutes — if green, we’ll proceed to 25%."
- "No SDK changes required for a model variant swap — same endpoint, different model id."
- "If you need geo-locking, we’ll scope the fallback to same-country regions or your Private deployment."

Status note: draft, needs legal to sign off on the billing template, and SRE to confirm on-call rollback semantics.

Related artifacts / references:
- Pilot checklist template (linked): CONFLUENCE-REDFX-42
- Past pilot war-room notes: JIRA-GTM-789
- Playbook PR with sample CLI: github.com/redwood-inference/rapid-playbook/pull/58

Notes to self: keep this intentionally short; add two real customer call transcripts next iteration; reconcile with 'fallback-simulation-sprint' doc so we don’t duplicate the post-mortem flows.

End of doc.
